name: Fiji
summary_text: Fiji is workable for trans visitors — the Pacific islands' leader. Same-sex relations decriminalised in 2010; the 2013 Constitution bans discrimination on the basis of gender identity AND expression — reportedly the only constitution in the world with that explicit pairing. Counterweights: no gender-marker change mechanism, and the Asia Pacific Transgender Network documents high rates of violence and harassment against trans people. Suva has an organised community (Haus of Khameleon, Rainbow Pride Foundation).

sources.title: Fiji | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations decriminalised 2010; Fiji's constitution bans discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression (2013 constitution, first enshrined 1997 - one of the first countries worldwide); workplace protections since 2007; health professionals prohibited from attempting to change sexual orientation; traditional third-gender population (vaka sa lewa lewa) but no legal gender recognition procedure.

sources.title: Policy Brief and Case Study: Legal Gender Recognition in Fiji - APA
sources.claim_summary: Asia Pacific Alliance policy brief and case study on legal gender recognition in Fiji (2023): despite the world-leading constitutional protection, legislative and policy frameworks do not permit gender-marker changes or recognise third-gender identities; trans people face high rates of violence, abuse and harassment and are marginalised in public, private and political sectors.

sources.title: Fiji: Sodomy Law Convictions Violate Constitution | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Apr 2005): 'Fiji: Sodomy Law Convictions Violate Constitution' — the prosecution and deportation of two men (one a tourist) under the 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature' law is unconstitutional.

sources.title: Fijian High Commission confirms; no more arrests for consensual gay sex in Fiji | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (July 2006): the Fijian High Commission confirmed men engaging in consensual gay sex would no longer be arrested - welcomed by the NZ AIDS Foundation as a step for human rights of 'gay citizens and tourists' and HIV prevention; notes Fiji's constitutional protections.

sources.title: Fiji - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz country report on Fiji: 1997 constitution was second in the world to protect against sexual-orientation discrimination; 2006 policy of not arresting men for consensual gay sex; legal since Feb 2010 under the Crimes Act; no same-sex marriage recognition (barred since 2002); 2011 president launched the UN 'Secret Lives, Other Voices' MSM/trans/HIV report.

sources.title: Fiji PM says homosexuality a sin
sources.claim_summary: Sydney Morning Herald (April 2005): Fiji's PM Laisenia Qarase rejected international pressure to legalise gay sex, calling homosexuality a sin - after an Australian tourist and a Fijian man received two-year jail sentences for sex; they were freed on bail pending appeal arguing the constitution's non-discrimination clause overrides the penal code.
